concepts.quote: 1,000,000, and if n doubles it runs twice as often.
concepts.why: 1,000,000 is right but given with no reasoning, so it only counts as L1. The prediction for the change is wrong: the inner loop runs all n passes on every outer pass, so doubling n makes count++ run 4 times as often, not 2.

concepts.quote: if n doubles it runs twice as often
concepts.why: The answer doesn't explain how the init, test and update fix the n×n passes, and the doubling claim is wrong (2n×2n = 4n²), so it can't reach L4.
The answer says nothing about i or j as loop variables.
The answer has nothing about a simulation or trial loop.
